paper_cards.title: SceneCode: Editable Indoor Scene Generation using Executable World Programs
paper_cards.data: indoor scene layouts and hierarchical scene-program examples covering generation, reconstruction, and local editing
paper_cards.method: hierarchical executable scene program that decomposes floor plans, rooms, and objects for editable scene generation
paper_cards.task: generate, reconstruct, and edit indoor scenes through executable world programs
paper_cards.novelty: treats indoor scene generation as structured executable program synthesis rather than opaque scene decoding
paper_cards.evidence: Primary paper plus official project page show the executable scene-code hierarchy and text/image/object-editing examples.

claim_checks.claim: Indoor scenes are represented as executable world programs
The representation decomposes scenes into floor-plan, room, and object programs
claim_checks.notes: Shown on the official project page.

paper_cards.limitations: Public evidence is strong on editable structure but lighter on simulator export and physical validation.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Good representation reference for structured world code, room-level scene decomposition, and local world edits.

paper_cards.title: SimWorld Studio: Generation and Evolution of Custom Embodied Agent Learning Environments
paper_cards.data: benchmark suite with 320 embodied tasks and 240 held-out layouts plus generated and evolved environment examples
paper_cards.method: environment generation-and-evolution loop that refines embodied learning worlds from user goals and feedback
paper_cards.task: generate and iteratively evolve custom embodied learning environments
paper_cards.novelty: extends embodied environment generation into an explicit closed-loop evolution process rather than one-shot PCG output
paper_cards.evidence: Official site and public code provide benchmark-scale evidence, generated-environment examples, and project framing.

claim_checks.claim: The benchmark suite contains 320 embodied tasks and 240 held-out layouts
claim_checks.notes: Reported on the official release page.

paper_cards.limitations: Portability beyond the supported environment stack remains less explicit than environment quality and task diversity.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Strong PCG baseline for custom embodied worlds, curriculum generation, and iterative environment refinement.

paper_cards.title: SpatialAct: Probing Spatial Reasoning-to-Action Capabilities of Vision-Language Models in 3D Scenes
paper_cards.data: 333 synthetic 3D scenes and 4,355 QA pairs across three reasoning-to-action task categories
paper_cards.method: 3D-scene benchmark with tool-based repair analysis for spatial reasoning-to-action
paper_cards.task: evaluate whether VLM spatial reasoning is useful for action-grounded decisions in 3D scenes
paper_cards.novelty: bridges spatial QA and action-grounded reasoning with a diagnostic repair stage and 3D benchmark design
paper_cards.evidence: Official project page provides benchmark counts, task taxonomy, and repair-agent framing.

claim_checks.claim: The benchmark contains 333 synthetic scenes and 4,355 QA pairs
claim_checks.notes: Reported on the official project page.

claim_checks.claim: SpatialAct targets spatial reasoning-to-action in 3D scenes

paper_cards.limitations: Benchmark conclusions depend on synthetic scene coverage and diagnostic task design.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Useful validator for spatial reasoning that must survive the jump from scene understanding to action-relevant decision making.

paper_cards.title: Cosmos-Predict2.5: A World Foundation Model for Physical AI
paper_cards.data: 200 million training video clips and official world-model release artifacts for physical-AI prediction
paper_cards.method: large action-conditioned world foundation model for future physical-scene prediction
paper_cards.task: predict physically meaningful future observations for control, planning, and simulation-like use cases
paper_cards.novelty: positions large-scale predictive world modeling directly as physical-AI infrastructure rather than generic video synthesis
paper_cards.evidence: Official NVIDIA release page exposes scale claims, release framing, and qualitative future-prediction demos.

claim_checks.claim: The release reports training on 200 million video clips
The model is framed as a world foundation model for physical AI

paper_cards.limitations: Public evidence is strong but still anchored to NVIDIA's official ecosystem and curated release materials.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Strong world-model baseline for action-conditioned rollout prediction and control-facing embodied generation.

paper_cards.title: A Unified Evaluation Harness for Vision-Language-Action Models
paper_cards.data: multi-benchmark VLA evaluation adapters, result reporting, and active official repository coverage
paper_cards.method: unified orchestration harness for running VLA models across multiple benchmark suites
paper_cards.task: evaluate VLA models consistently across benchmarks and execution stacks
paper_cards.novelty: standardizes VLA benchmarking infrastructure instead of leaving evaluation fragmented across project-specific scripts
paper_cards.evidence: The paper and official repository together provide a clean infrastructure story and active release surface.

claim_checks.claim: The paper snapshot reports 13 benchmarks and 657 published results
claim_checks.notes: Use only for the paper snapshot.

claim_checks.claim: Official code is public and the repository acts as a living implementation
claim_checks.notes: Repository is public and actively documented.

paper_cards.limitations: Exact benchmark counts are date-sensitive after release and depend on the underlying benchmark suites.
paper_cards.project_relevance: High-value infrastructure reference for evaluation adapters, result schemas, and standardized VLA benchmarking.

paper_cards.title: VLA-REPLICA: A Low-Cost, Reproducible Benchmark for Real-World Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Models
paper_cards.data: low-cost real-world VLA benchmark setup with 10 tasks, demonstration data, and reproducibility checks across independently built setups
paper_cards.method: standardized physical setup and evaluation protocol for reproducible real-world VLA benchmarking
paper_cards.task: measure VLA performance in a replicable real-world robot setting with ID and OOD evaluation
paper_cards.novelty: prioritizes affordability and cross-site reproducibility in real-world VLA evaluation
paper_cards.evidence: Primary paper and official project page describe the hardware, task suite, and reproducibility framing in enough detail for acceptance.

claim_checks.claim: The benchmark uses off-the-shelf components and targets reproducible real-world VLA evaluation
claim_checks.notes: Stated on the official project page.

paper_cards.limitations: Task scope is intentionally smaller than the largest simulation benchmarks and hardware is centered on a specific low-cost setup.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Useful template for low-cost, reproducible real-world evaluation of action models and embodied policies.
